findings.issue: Family punctuation split, cosmetic. The two user forms keep the comma apposition INSIDE the parentheses the translator added (跳转到你的消息（第{turn}轮，共{total}轮）) while checkpoint.turn, jump_agent and jump_agent_unnamed spell the same pair as 第{turn}轮（共{total}轮）. Both are idiomatic Chinese progress forms (compare 第3页（共12页）), checkpoint-model.ts deliberately delegates each sentence's spelling to the catalogue ('the noun and its word order belong to the catalogue', checkpointTurnLabel docstring), and the comma form avoids nesting a second parenthetical inside the destination bracket — so the translator's declination is defensible and this is not a meaning, accuracy or grammar defect. Recorded because the manager asked for the judgement, not because the current text needs a change.

findings.issue: Code-level, inherited. {clock} is filled by checkpointClockLabel(), which hardcodes the English 12-hour 'h:mm a' shape ('12-hour with an AM/PM marker by request', checkpoint-model.ts). The zh-CN style guide requires 24-hour times ("14:30") and this key's own sidecar promises "{clock} is a clock time already formatted by the locale-aware time formatter". Measured with the real builder: 跳转到你的消息（第3轮，共12轮），3:45 PM. The Chinese sentence is correct; the English-shaped time comes from the formatter, not the catalogue, and the same hardcoded shape is product-wide (formatMessageDateTime), so this does not gate the translation. Same class as the fr audit's fr-wavea-3.
findings.current: 跳转到你的消息（第{turn, number}轮，共{total, number}轮），{clock}
findings.proposed: (no catalogue change) format {clock} through the locale-aware 24-hour formatter for zh-CN (14:45) in checkpointClockLabel / formatMessageDateTime
findings.proposed_note: Belongs in the formatter; the catalogue value stays as it is.

findings.issue: Verified-OK; the wave-A MAJOR (M1) is resolved. chatRegionLabel() rendered through the shipped runtime returns 对话 for sidebar (ui.chat.sidebar.nav.chats), 对话区 for header/transcript (ui.chat.region.conversation) and 消息输入框 for composer (ui.chat.region.composer) — three distinct names, so the sidebar nav and the transcript landmark no longer announce identically. The header <header> carries no aria-label by design (chat-header.tsx: 'NO aria-label ... this is not one of §C4's named three'), so the announced set in this tree is exactly 对话 / 对话区 / 消息输入框. 对话区 is natural product Chinese: 区 is the region word this catalogue already uses (ui.settings.shortcuts.reserved.chat_region_down/up say 对话区域 for the generic plural 'chat regions'; the pickers use 分析区域, 上下文估算区域, 会话诊断区域), but those translate an English 'X region' while this key translates bare 'Conversation'; 对话区 names the place in three characters and fits the guide's terse rule. 对话区域 would also pass and would match the sibling region labels more formally — a preference, not a defect, so no change is proposed.

Verified-OK. 消息输入框 names the message box rather than the whole composer <form> (which also holds the status row, alert band and interrupt notice — the same narrowing the fr audit noted as fr-wavea-2), but it is this catalogue's existing word for that area (ui.chat.question_dock.hint.approval_held: 也可以在消息输入框中按Esc停止本轮) and the region's data-region-entry is the textarea itself, so the name a reader hears on landing is truthful. No change.

Verified-OK; answers the manager's question. 回答操作 (Answer actions), 回复操作 (Response actions, pre-existing ui.chat.response_actions.label), 叙述操作 (Commentary actions) and 你的消息操作 (Your message actions) are four different names in one conversation. 回答操作 and 回复操作 share the first syllable 回 but differ in the second (dá vs fù) and are separate words, not a near-duplicate: 回复 is this catalogue's established word for a 'response' (ui.settings.appearance.transcript_display_mode_setting.by_response = 按回复, which 'keeps every settled response'), and 回答 is its word for an answer (ui.notices.chat.answer_changed = 回答已更新; ui.chat.asks.send_answer = 发送回答). The one-character difference therefore encodes the product's own answer/response split that the English sidecar requires these two toolbars to keep distinct, and a screen reader announces each as a whole name on its own row. Acceptable distinctness; no change.
